title: Erdős #31: Primes Have Natural Density Zero
description: Proves primes have natural density zero: |{primes ≤ N}| / N → 0 as N → ∞. Uses Chebyshev's theta bound θ(N) ≤ N·log(4) and the prime counting estimate π(N) ≤ 2N·log(4)/log(N) + √N + 1. 9 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: That primes have density zero (π(N)/N → 0) follows from Chebyshev's estimates. The Prime Number Theorem gives the sharper π(N) ~ N/log(N), but density zero follows from the elementary θ(N) ≤ N·log(4).
overview.problemStatement: Prove the natural density of the prime numbers is 0: |{p ≤ N : p prime}| / N → 0.
overview.proofStrategy: chebyshevTheta_le: θ(N) ≤ N·log(4) (from primorial bound). primeCounting_le_chebyshev: π(N) ≤ 2N·log(4)/log(N) + √N + 1. chebyshev_bound_tendsto_zero: the bound tends to 0. primes_density_zero follows.
keyInsights: **Chebyshev's theta bound**: θ(N) = Σ_{p≤N} log p ≤ N·log(4) follows from the primorial (product of primes ≤ N) being at most 4^N.
**Prime counting estimate**: π(N) ≤ θ(N)/log(√N) + O(√N) since each prime p > √N contributes log(p) > log(√N) to θ.
**Density zero**: combining these, π(N)/N ≤ 2·log(4)/log(N) + 1/√N → 0, so primes have density 0 without PNT.
